description: Design the smallest justified execution graph for a human-agent system with typed nodes and edges, explicit authority, bounded state, recovery, termination, and independent proof.

positive: A human-agent system needs explicit dependencies, branches, joins, handoffs, approval gates, or recovery paths.
Different work nodes require distinct capabilities, permissions, data scopes, budgets, or independent verification.
negative: A single deterministic function, bounded skill, or sequential loop can produce and verify the result.
The request is only for a capability graph, GraphRAG index, database choice, dependency visualization, or decorative diagram.

procedure.instruction: Compare a deterministic workflow, one agent loop, sequential skill composition, and an execution graph before choosing the system shape.
procedure.proof: A rejected-complexity ledger justifies or refuses graph structure.

procedure.instruction: Define typed task, router, join, gate, checkpoint, and terminal nodes independently from executor choice.
procedure.proof: Every node owns one result or policy boundary and every reference resolves.

procedure.instruction: Type dependency, control, data, handoff, approval, recovery, and compensation edges so delegated authority can only attenuate.
procedure.proof: All nodes are reachable, joins are deterministic, and consequential actions traverse human gates.

procedure.instruction: Specify state, checkpoints, idempotency, retry classes, replay frontier, compensation, termination, wall time, parallelism, and spend.
procedure.proof: Every failure class reaches recovery, escalation, or a bounded terminal state.

procedure.instruction: Bind each node to the least-powerful viable executor and require persistent-agent controls only where a durable boundary is proven.
procedure.proof: Capability coverage is complete and false agent boundaries are downgraded.

procedure.instruction: Compare the graph with the simplest viable baseline across structural, behavioral, recovery, authority, provenance, economic, and independent-defense lanes.
procedure.proof: A receipt records passed, failed, pending, and unresolved evidence without activation.

inputs: Task Envelope, objective, beneficiary, constraints, and accountable human
Available skills, tools, temporary workers, and attested agent builds
Input, output, state, event, policy, budget, and data contracts
Required behavioral, recovery, security, economic, and independent-evaluation lanes
outputs: Node, edge, capability, authority, state, and budget contracts
Failure, recovery, observability, and evaluation plan
Proof receipt with unresolved promotion evidence
